title: Normalisation: batch, layer, and why it makes training stable

videos.script: A network of ten layers learns the digits well at a learning rate of 0.03. {{slow}} Raise the rate to 0.1, and it climbs for ten epochs and then falls apart. {{collapse}} At 1.0 it learns nothing at all. This lesson is about the layer that stops that. {{title}} It starts at the front of the network. Feed it the raw ink levels, from zero to sixteen, and rates that worked stop working. {{scale}} Batch normalisation takes the same fix inside the network. At every layer, each feature is brought to mean zero and variance one, over the batch. {{bn}} You will write it for tinynet, forward and backward, and check its gradient. With it, the ten-layer network trains at every rate that broke it. {{deep}} It has a price. A layer that measures the batch misbehaves when there is no batch. Predict one image in training mode, and every image gets the same answer. {{bug}} Layer normalisation does the same arithmetic along the other axis, one example at a time. {{ln}} Nothing in it depends on the batch, and that is why the transformers of lesson 15 use it. {{end}}
